questions.q: An ideal gas is expanding such that $PT^{3} =$ constant. The coefficient of volume expansion of the gas is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\gamma = \dfrac{1}{V}\dfrac{dV}{dt}$

$PT^{3} =$ constant

$\dfrac{T}{V}T^{3} =$ Constant

$T^{4}V^{- 1} = C$

$V^{- 1}\left(4T^{3}dT\right) + T^{4}\left(\dfrac{- 1}{V2}dV\right) = 0$

$\dfrac{dV}{dT} = \dfrac{4T^{3} / V}{T^{4} / V^{2}} = \dfrac{4V}{T} ∴ \gamma = \dfrac{4}{T}$

questions.q:
$1$ kg~of water, at $20 ° C$ is heated in an electric kettle whose heating element has a mean (temperature averaged) resistance of $20Ω .$ The rms voltage in the mains is $200V$. Ignoring heat loss from the kettle, time taken for water to evaporate fully is close to
[ Specific heat of water $= 4200J{kg}^{- 1} ° C^{- 1}$ Latent heat of water $= 2260kJkg^{- 1}$ ]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given specific heat of the water $4200J{kg}^{- 1} ° C^{- 1}$

Latent heat of the water $= 2260kJkg^{- 1}$

$Q = P \times t$

$Q = mc\Delta T + mL$

$⇒ P \times t = mc\Delta T + mL$

$⇒ \dfrac{{V}_{rms}^{2}}{R} \times t = mc\Delta T + mL$

$⇒ \dfrac{{\left(200\right)}^{2}}{20} \times t = 4200 \times 80 + 2260 \times {10}^{3}$

$⇒ t = 1298\text{s} ≃ 22min$

questions.q: Two metallic wires of identical dimensions are connected is series. If ${σ}_{1}$ and ${σ}_{2}$ are the conductivities of the these wires respectively, the effective conductivity of the combination is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let length of wire be $l$,
Area of wire as $A$
For equivalent wire length $= 2l$~& area will be $A$

As the wires are connected in series combination, the thermal resistance

${R}_{eq} = {R}_{1} + {R}_{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{2l}{{σ}_{eq}A} = \dfrac{l}{{σ}_{1}A} + \dfrac{l}{{σ}_{1}A}$

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{\sigmaeq} = \dfrac{1}{\sigma1} + \dfrac{1}{\sigma2} ⇒ {σ}_{eq} = \dfrac{2{σ}_{1}{σ}_{2}}{{σ}_{1} + {σ}_{2}}$

questions.q: Two different wires having lengths ${L}_{1}$ and ${L}_{2}$ and respective temperature coefficient of linear expansion~${α}_{1}$~and~${α}_{2},$ are joined end-to-end. Then the effective temperature coefficient of linear expansion is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The wire are joined end-to-end, so they are in series combination, then total& length of wire is given by
$L = {L}_{1} + {L}_{2} . . . ( 1 )$

When the temperature is increase by~$∆ \theta$, then its final length is given by using concept of linear expansion,
$L^{'} = L ( 1 + \alpha ∆ \theta ) . . . ( 2 )$

Using equation $( 1 )$ and $( 2 )$ for the series combination of wires, final length is given by

$L^{'} = {L1}^{'} + {L2}^{'} . . . ( 3 )$

$⇒ \left({L}_{1} + {L}_{2}\right) ( 1 + {α}_{eff} ∆ \theta ) = {L}_{1} ( 1 + {α}_{1} ∆ \theta ) + {L}_{2} ( 1 + {α}_{2} ∆ \theta )$

$⇒ {α}_{eff} = {L}_{1}{α}_{1} + {L}_{2}{α}_{2} \left({L}_{1} + {L}_{2}\right)

$

questions.q:
Heat energy of $184kJ$~is given to ice of mass $600g$ at $- 12 ° C$, Specific heat of ice is $2222 . 3J{kg}^{– 1} ° C^{– 1}$ and latent heat of ice is~$336kJ{kg}^{– 1}$.

(A) Final temperature of system will be $0 ° C$

(B) Final temperature of the system will be greater than $0 ° C$

(C) The final system will have a mixture of ice and water in the ratio of $5: 1$

(D) The final system will have a mixture of ice and water in the ratio of~ $1: 5$

(E) The final system will have water only

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:

$∆ Q = 184 \times {10}^{3}J$,

$m = 0 . 600kg\text{at} - 12 ° C$,

$S = 2222 . 3J{kg}^{– 1} ° C^{– 1}$~and

$L = 336 \times {10}^{3}J{kg}^{- 1}$

Heat required to convert ice from~$– 12 ° C$ to ice at~$0 ° C$~will be,~

${Q}_{1} = 0 . 600 \times 2222 . 3 \times 12 = 16000 . 56J$

Remaining heat~$Q = 184000 - 16000 . 56$

$= 167999 . 44J$

Heat required to melt ice completely at~$0 ° C$,

${Q}_{2} = 0 . 600 \times 336000 = 201600J$~needed which is more than~$Q$, so~$100 %$~ice is not melted.

For amount of melted ice, we can write

$167999 . 44 = m \times 336000 ⇒ m = 0 . 4999kg$

$∴$~mass of water~$= 0 . 4999kg$

Mass of ice remaining~$= 0 . 1001$

$∴$~Ratio~$= \dfrac{0 . 1001}{0 . 4999} \approx 1: 5$

questions.q: A $100g$~of iron nail is hit by a $1 . 5kg$ hammer striking at a velocity of $60\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$. What will be the rise in the temperature of the nail if one fourth of energy of the hammer goes into heating the nail ? [Specific heat capacity of iron $= 0 . 42{Jg}^{- 1}{C ∘}^{- 1}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If we heat-up an object, then, the& energy is used to either change the temperature of the body or to change the state of the body.
If it& changes the temperature, then,

$Q = mS ∆ T$
where,~$Q$~is the heat given,~$m$~is the mass and~$∆ T$~is the change in temperature.

We know that a moving object has~an energy in the form of kinetic energy, i.e.,
$KE = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}$

When that moving object strikes another object,~it~loses some energy which~changes into the heat~energy and this heat energy increases the temperature of the object.
Given~a hammer of~$1 . 5kg$~is moving with~$60ms^{- 1}$.
Kinetic energy~$= \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} ( 1 . 5 ) ( 60{)}^{2} = 2700J$
One-fourth of kinetic energy changes into heat energy.
$⇒ \dfrac{1}{4} ( KE ) =$~Heat energy
$⇒ \dfrac{1}{4} ( KE ) = m ( S ) ( ∆ T )$
$⇒ \dfrac{1}{4} ( 2700 ) = ( 100 ) ( 0 . 42 ) ( ∆ T )$
$⇒ ∆ T = 16 . 07 ° C$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion $A$~and the other is labelled as Reason $R$.

Assertion $A$~: When a rod lying freely is heated, no thermal stress is developed in it.

Reason $R$& :& On heating, the length of the rod increases.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both& $A$ and~$R$ are true and $R$~is the correct explanation of~$A$
Both $A$~and $R$~are true but $R$~is NOT~the correct explanation of~$A$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Thermal stress is mechanical stress created by any change in temperature of a material. When the body is under some constraints, thermal stress is generated. But if it is lying freely, no thermal stress is developed.

The increase in length of a body with& temperature is given by

$∆ L = L\alpha ∆ T$

So, with the increase in temperature, the length of the rod increases.

$A$~and $R$~are true but $R$~is not the correct explanation of $A$.

questions.q: Two conductors have the same resistances at $0 ° C$ but their temperature coefficients of resistance are ${α}_{1}$ and ${α}_{2}$. The respective temperature coefficients for their series and parallel combinations are :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Change in resistance due to temperature is given by, $R^{'} = R \left(1 + \alpha∆ T\right)$

For Series Combination:

${R}_{eq} = {R}_{1} + {R}_{2}$

$⇒ 2R \left(1 + {α}_{eq} ∆ T\right) = R \left(1 + {α}_{1} ∆ T\right) + R\left(1 + {α}_{2} ∆ T\right)$

$⇒ 2R\left(1 + {α}_{eq} ∆ T\right) = 2R + \left({α}_{1} + {α}_{2}\right)R ∆ T$

$⇒ {α}_{eq} = $\dfrac{{α}_{1} + {α}_{2}}{2}

For Parallel Combination:

\dfrac{1}{Req} = \dfrac{1}{R1} + \dfrac{1}{R2}

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{\dfrac{R}{2}\left(1 + {α}_{eq} ∆ T\right)} = \dfrac{1}{R\left(1 + {α}_{1} ∆ T\right)} + \dfrac{1}{R\left(1 + {α}_{2} ∆ T\right)}

$⇒ $\dfrac{2}{1 + {α}_{eq} ∆ T} = \dfrac{1}{1 + {α}_{1} ∆ T} + \dfrac{1}{1 + {α}_{2} ∆ T}

$⇒ $\dfrac{2}{1 + {α}_{eq} ∆ T} = \dfrac{1 + {α}_{2} ∆ T + 1 + {α}_{1} ∆ T}{ \left(1 + {α}_{1} ∆ T\right)\left(1 + {α}_{2} ∆ T\right)}$

$⇒ 2\left[\left(1 + {α}_{1} ∆ T\right)\left($1 + {α}_{2} ∆ T\right)\right] = \left[$2 + \left({α}_{1} + {α}_{2}\right)∆ T\right]\left[1 + {α}_{eq} ∆ T\right]$

$⇒ 2\left[1 + {α}_{1} ∆ T + {α}_{2} ∆ T + {α}_{1}{α}_{2} ∆ T\right] = 2 + 2{α}_{eq} ∆ T + \left({α}_{1} + {α}_{2}\right)∆ T + {α}_{eq}\left({α}_{1} + {α}_{2}\right)∆ T^{2}$

Neglecting small terms

$2 + 2\left({α}_{1} + {α}_{2}\right)∆ T = 2 + 2{α}_{eq} ∆ T + \left({α}_{1} + {α}_{2}\right)∆ T$

$⇒ \left({α}_{1} + {α}_{2}\right)∆ T = 2{α}_{eq} ∆ T$

$⇒ {α}_{eq} = \dfrac{{α}_{1} + {α}_{2}}{2}$

$

questions.q: A block of ice at $- 10 ° C$ is slowly heated and converted to steam at $100 ° C$. Which of the following curves represent the phenomenon qualitatively:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When the state of the substance is not changing, temperature of the substance increases when heat is supplied to it. But when the substance changes the state, the heat supplied to it used as latent heat and the temperature remains constant until all the substance converts to other state.

Therefore, temperature of ice first increases from $- 10 ° C$ to $0 ° C$. Then, remains constant at $0 ° C$ till whole ice is melted. Then, it increases from $0 ° C$ to $100 ° C$. Again it remains constant at $100 ° C$ till whole water converts into steam.

questions.q: Two thin metallic spherical shells of radii ${r}_{1}$ and ${r}_{2}  \left({r}_{1}< {r}_{2}\right)$ are placed with their centres coinciding. A material of thermal conductivity $K$ is filled in the space between the shells. The inner shell is maintained at temperature ${θ}_{1}$ and the outer shell at temperature ${θ}_{2}\left({θ}_{1}$< {θ}_{2}\right) .$& The rate at which heat flows radially through the material is :$

questions.solution:
Equivalent resistance $( R ) = \dfrac{{r}_{2} - {r}_{1}}{K4\pi{r}_{2}{r}_{1}}$
Thus, Heat flow $= 4\piK \left({r}_{1}{r}_{2}\right) \left({θ}_{2} - {θ}_{1}\right) \left({r}_{2} - {r}_{1}\right)$

questions.q: If ${K}_{1}$~and ${K}_{2}$ are the thermal conductivities ${L}_{1}$ and ${L}_{2}$ are the lengths and ${A}_{1}$ and ${A}_{2}$ are the cross sectional areas of steel and copper rods respectively such that $\dfrac{K2}{K1} = 9, \dfrac{A1}{A2} = 2, \dfrac{L1}{L2} = 2$. Then, for the arrangement as shown in the figure. The value of temperature $T$ of the steel - copper junction in the steady state will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At steady state, the& heat conducted by both the rods will be the same.

The rate& of heat conduction is given by,& $\dfrac{d Q}{d t} = \dfrac{KA}{l} ∆ T$. Therefore, if the temperature of the junction is~$T$,

$\dfrac{{K}_{1}{A}_{1}}{l1} \left({T}_{1} -T\right) = $\dfrac{{K}_{2}{A}_{2}}{l2}\left($T - {T}_{2}\right)$

$⇒ $\dfrac{450 - T}{T - 0} = \dfrac{{K}_{2}{A}_{2}{l}_{1}}{{K}_{1}{A}_{1}{l}_{2}} =$9 \times $\dfrac{1}{2} \times$2$

$⇒ 450 - T = 9T ⇒ T = 45 ° C

$

questions.q: On a temperature scale '$X$', the boiling point of water is $65 ° X$ and the freezing point is $- 15 ° X$. Assuming that the $X$~scale is linear. The equivalent temperature corresponding to $- 95 ° X$ on the Fahrenheit scale would be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The relation between two temperature scales can be written as follows

$\dfrac{65 - x}{65 - \left(-15\right)} = $\dfrac{212 - F}{180} . . . \left($1\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters in to equation (1) and sole to calculate the required temperature in Fahrenheit scale.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{65 + 95}{80}& = & \dfrac{212 - F}{180}\\ & ⇒ & 2 \times180 = 212 - F \\ & ⇒ & F = 212 - 360 \\ & = & - 148 ° F\end{cases}$$

$

questions.q: A faulty thermometer reads $5 ° C$~in melting ice and $95 ° C$~in steam. The correct temperature on absolute scale will be ______ $K$ when the faulty thermometer reads~$41 ° C$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As per& working of thermometers,& $\dfrac{X - LFP}{UFP - LFP} = \text{constant}$.

Therefore, we can write

~$\dfrac{41 ° - 5 °}{95 ° - 5 °} = \dfrac{C - 0 °}{100 ° - 0 °}$

$⇒ C = \dfrac{36}{90} \times 100 = 40 ° C = 40 + 273K = 313K$

questions.q: A bakelite beaker has volume capacity of& $500cc$ at $30 ° C$. When it is partially filled with~${V}_{m}$ volume (at~$30 ° C$)~ of mercury, it is found that the unfilled volume of the beaker remains constant as temperature is varied. If~${γ}_{bester } = 6 \times {10}^{- 6}0 ° C^{- 1},$ where~$\gamma$ is the coefficient of volume expansion, then ${V}_{m}$ (in $cc$ ) is close to $\ldots$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$∆ Vm = ∆ Vc$

$Vm \gamma m ∆ T = Vc \gamma c ∆ T$

$Vm = \dfrac{Vcγc}{γm} = \dfrac{500 \times 6 \times {10}^{- 6}}{1 . 5 . \times {10}^{- 4}} = 20cc$

questions.q:
A geyser heats water flowing at a rate of $2 . 0kg$ per minute from $30 ° C$ to $70 ° C$. If geyser operates on a gas burner, the rate of combustion of fuel will be _____~$g\min^{- 1}$.

[Heat of combustion $= 8 \times {10}^{3}{Jg}^{- 1}$, Specific heat of water $= 4 . 2{Jg}^{- 1}{C ∘}^{- 1}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here, mass flow rate of water,& $\dfrac{d m}{d t} = 2kg\min^{- 1}$

The geyser heats the water, raising the temperature from~${θ}_{1} = 30 ° C$~to~${θ}_{2} = 70 ° C$.

Total heat utilised in raising the temperature,~$\dfrac{\Delta Q}{\Deltat} = \dfrac{d m}{d t} \times s\Delta\theta$

$\dfrac{\Delta Q}{\Deltat} = \dfrac{2}{60} \times 4 . 2 \times 40 = \dfrac{m}{t} \times L$

$L =$ heat of combination$= 8 \times {10}^{3}Jg^{- 1}$

Now, rate of consumption of fuel is~$\dfrac{m}{t} = \dfrac{2 \times 4 . 2 \times 40}{60 \times 8 \times {10}^{3}}$

$= \dfrac{4 . 2}{6} \times {10}^{- 3} = 0 . 7 \times {10}^{- 3}kg\sec^{- 1}$

$= 42g\min^{- 1}$

questions.q:
Two cylindrical rods A and B made of different materials, are joined in a straight line. The ratio of lengths, radii and thermal conductivities of these rods are :
$\frac{\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\frac{1}{2}, \frac{\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{B}}}=2$ and $\frac{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\frac{1}{2}$. The free ends of rods A and B are maintained at $400 \mathrm{~K}, 200 \mathrm{~K}$, respectively. The temperature of rods interface is ________ K, when equilibrium is established.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{R}_1=\frac{\ell_1}{\mathrm{~K}_1 \mathrm{~A}_1}, \mathrm{R}_2=\frac{\ell_2}{\mathrm{~K}_2 \mathrm{~A}_2} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{dQ}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{T}}{\mathrm{R}} \\ & \left(\frac{\mathrm{dQ}}{\mathrm{dt}}\right)_1=\left(\frac{\mathrm{dQ}}{\mu}\right)_2 \\ & \frac{400-\mathrm{T}}{\mathrm{R}_1}=\frac{\mathrm{T}-200}{\mathrm{R}_2} \\ & \frac{400-\mathrm{T}}{\mathrm{T}-200}=\frac{\mathrm{R}_1}{\mathrm{R}_2}=\left(\frac{\ell_1}{\ell_2}\right)\left(\frac{\mathrm{r}_2}{\mathrm{r}_1}\right)^2 \times \frac{\mathrm{K}_2}{\mathrm{~K}_1} \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \times\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 \times 2 \\ & =\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) \\ & \frac{400-\mathrm{T}}{\mathrm{T}-200}=\frac{1}{4} \\ & 1600-4 \mathrm{~T}=\mathrm{T}-200 \\ & 5 \mathrm{~T}=1800 \\ & \mathrm{~T}=360 \mathrm{~K}\end{aligned}$
